question: What time (in seconds) is required for a 398 m long train to cross a 802 m long tunnel, if the train travels at a speed of 45 km/h?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cover = Length of train + Length of tunnel = 398 + 802 = 1200 m

Speed in m/s = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s

Time = Total distance ÷ Speed = 1200 ÷ 12.5 = 96 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 96 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the train (L₁) = 398 m

Length of the tunnel (L₂) = 802 m

Speed of the train (S) = 45 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Tunnel

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 398 + 802 = 1200 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 45 × (5/18) = 25/2 = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Time required = 1200 ÷ 12.5

⇒ Time required = 96 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 96 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Speed

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by (5/18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18/5).

Crossing a Stationary Object with Length

When a train crosses a tunnel, bridge, or a standing platform, the total distance covered to clear the object is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the object.

Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, a stationary man, or a tree, the total distance covered to clear it is only equal to the length of the train itself.
